metadata.method: Fresh process per case/build/round; first-use collections retained separately; two extra warmups per engine; alternating CPU/Metal timed order; process/build order rotated per round; inputs and exact CPU-reference validation untimed; complete result materialization timed; result release untimed.
metadata.scope: Development mechanisms only, not external-suite evidence or a general GPU speedup. Chain32 includes fusion advantages over the current CPU executor.
metadata.data: Row mechanisms use a deterministic 1024-value numeric distribution. Algorithm cases use Int32 keys: group_hash and group_skew have min(N,1024) classes; group_high, join_hash and sort_radix have max(1,N/2) classes; join_fanout uses ceil(N/4) cyclic or monotone balanced classes, so each key occurs at most four times and a self-left-join emits at most 4N rows. Base non-fanout keys are (37*i) modulo cardinality; sorted keys are monotone bins. group_skew maps three quarters of rows to key zero. Null variants invalidate every twentieth key; grouped values additionally invalidate every thirteenth row. Grouped sums use i modulo 17 minus 8; sort and self-left-join carry original Int64 row IDs. Float32 row values are exact multiples of 1/1024. Float64 arithmetic uses exact binary fractions k/1024 with k in [0,1023] and evaluates x*2+0.25. Decimal input is Decimal(15,2) cents with unscaled values in [-8,8]; the query multiplies by Decimal(15,2) 1.25 then sums. Wide Float32 projects eight columns with binary-exact offsets [0,0.125,...,0.875], at most 8N output values or 256 MiB at the default 8,388,608 rows.
limitations: No external-suite coverage claimed. Floating reductions remain outside these cases. Algorithm comparisons preserve complete output order and values against CPU; this CPU check is not an independent oracle.
First use includes context/shader initialization but is not a cold machine or cold filesystem measurement.
CPU and GPU share host memory and power limits; short timings can vary with scheduler and thermal state.

The Mojo profile is a separate warm collection after timed samples; complete caller-wall timing remains the performance measure. Reported host phase timings are retained as measured and may overlap; they are not added. GPU-only time and pipeline compilation attribution are unavailable unless the runtime supplies those fields.
Workload exposure: chain32 was used during fusion development; other cases broaden mechanism coverage without a holdout claim.

Power and thermal snapshots use read-only pmset queries when available. Missing commands, unsupported output, and timeouts are retained as unavailable; the snapshot is context, not a controlled power measurement.
